verdict.rationale: TruffleHog documents that for every secret type it can classify, it can log in to confirm whether the secret is live. It exposes this through CLI flags such as `--only-verified` and `--results=verified,unknown`, per-detector verification overrides (`--verify-detectors`/`--no-verify-detectors`), and webhook-based verification for custom regex detectors. The capability appears consistently across the GitHub README and the docs. missing for 10: independent or hands-on corroboration that verification works accurately in practice.

support.subject: As a security-engineer, I can have detected secrets verified against the issuing service so I know which ones are live

citations.quote: For every secret TruffleHog can classify, it can also log in to confirm if that secret is live or not.
the `--verify-detectors` and `--no-verify-detectors` CLI flags can be used to configure detector-specific verification override settings
Verification is done via a webhook POST request to the provided `endpoint`.
